title: Graded tensor-adjunction evaluation and its ordinary-scheme normalization
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $T$ a scheme over $S$ [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism over $S$ that is quasi-compact and separated [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. Regard $T$ as its representable algebraic space [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Use the small etale module direct image and tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $(B_d)_{d\geq0}$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], with $\mathcal O_X$-bilinear homogeneous products $B_m\otimes B_n\to B_{m+n}$ and a unit $\mathcal O_X\to B_0$, compatible with restrictions and satisfying associativity, ordinary commutativity, and the unit laws. Tensor products mean sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; the total graded object is the coproduct in module sheaves, not an assertion that sections on every open commute with infinite coproducts. Put $A_d=(f_*B_d)|_{T_{\mathrm{Zar}}}$, using the quasi-coherent Zariski/small-etale equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], and give $\bigoplus_d A_d$ its products of compatible sections [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. For each $d$ the map $\epsilon_d:f^*(A_d)_{\mathrm{et}}\to B_d$ adjunct to the identity of $f_*B_d$ is the evaluation with local tensor formula $a\otimes s\mapsto a\,s|_W$, whenever an etale chart $W\to X$ lies over the domain of the section $s$. These degree maps assemble, through the canonical coproduct comparison $f^*(\bigoplus_d(A_d)_{\mathrm{et}})\simeq\bigoplus_d f^*(A_d)_{\mathrm{et}}$, to a homomorphism of commutative unital graded algebras $\epsilon:f^*(\bigoplus_d(A_d)_{\mathrm{et}})\to\bigoplus_d B_d$. It satisfies $\epsilon((a\otimes s)(b\otimes t))=ab\,(st)|_W=(a\,s|_W)(b\,t|_W)$ and sends the unit to the unit. Suppose additionally that $X$ is a scheme and $B_d\simeq(H_d)_{\mathrm{et}}$ for quasi-coherent Zariski modules $H_d$, with their homogeneous products transported by this equivalence. Then the identity-on-open-sections comparisons identify $A_d$ with the ordinary Zariski direct image $f_*H_d$, identify all homogeneous products and units, and identify $\epsilon_d$ with the ordinary Zariski tensor-pullback counit under the pullback comparison [def-pc-module-pullback]. The same holds for the coproduct evaluation. If $B_d=L^{\otimes d}$ for a line module, the $H_d$ are the tensor powers, including the zeroth power, of the ordinary invertible module corresponding to $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module]; their identifications respect the canonical tensor-power products.

source.place: Tag 0D3C (lemma-descending-property-ample), proof: the natural maps psi_d and their graded sum psi; the ordinary-scheme interpretation is the representable-pushforward discussion preceding spaces-morphisms.tex lemma-pushforward. The tensor adjunction is sites-modules.tex lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; the Zariski/etale comparison is descent.tex proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial (1),(3).

proof.text: Put $C_d=f_*B_d$. Apply [lem-trf-graded-qc-section-algebra-construction] to the given family. It gives the quasi-coherence of $A_d$, the specified isomorphisms $(A_d)_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq C_d$ equal to the identity on open sections, and the graded products and unit on their sheaf coproducts. Here $T$ carries its given $S$-structure, $f$ is over $S$, and its target is the specified representable algebraic space. Thus its base-scheme hypotheses as well as quasi-compactness, separatedness, quasi-coherence and homogeneous algebra laws hold. In the remaining steps identify $(A_d)_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $C_d$ by these fixed maps; thus a section $s$ of $C_d$ means a compatible family of chart sections, and $s|_W$ means its specified chart projection.

source.place: Tag 0D3C, lemma-descending-property-ample, section-algebra paragraph; degreewise construction already isolated in the cited node.

proof.text: Let $\epsilon_d:f^*C_d\to B_d$ be the counit of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. The triangle identity is $f_*\epsilon_d\circ\eta_{C_d}=1_{C_d}$. Project this equality to the chart $(W,a)$ over an etale test scheme $V\to T$. Naturality of chart projections in module maps gives $\epsilon_d(\pi_{W,a}(\eta_{C_d}(s)))=\pi_{W,a}(s)$. By $\mathcal O_X$-linearity, $\epsilon_d(a\,\pi_{W,a}(\eta(s)))=a\,s|_W$. The unit-normalized isomorphism of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] identifies the input with the local sheaf tensor $a\otimes s$. It also realizes these as the usual sheafified tensor construction, so their local finite sums determine the map; no global section is assumed to be a pure tensor. This proves the claimed evaluation formula for the actual adjunction counit.

source.place: Tag 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; counit formula by the triangle identity and the chart-unit tensor normalization.

proof.text:
The coproduct comparison follows directly from the adjunction of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]: for any target module $H$,
$\operatorname{Hom}(f^*(\bigoplus_dC_d),H)=\operatorname{Hom}(\bigoplus_dC_d,f_*H)=\prod_d\operatorname{Hom}(C_d,f_*H)=\prod_d\operatorname{Hom}(f^*C_d,H)$.
Thus $f^*(\bigoplus_dC_d)$ has the coproduct universal property, with injections $f^*\iota_d$. The inverse comparison to $\bigoplus_df^*C_d$ is the unique map preserving these injections. Define $\epsilon$ by the component maps $\iota_d\epsilon_d$ using this universal property. Likewise, the tensor/Hom adjunction of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] gives
$\operatorname{Hom}(M\otimes\bigoplus_dN_d,H)=\prod_d\operatorname{Hom}(M\otimes N_d,H)$.
By symmetry this holds in either tensor variable. Hence maps from the tensor of two such coproducts are determined by the pairs of homogeneous summands. These are statements about sheaf coproducts, not about sums of sections on an arbitrary open.

source.place: Tag 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; tensor/Hom adjunction, with the displayed coproduct universal-property calculation.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison-construction] with the ringed tensor pullback of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization]. The normalization in [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison] sends the unit-inserted tensor of $s,t$ to the tensor of their unit insertions. Consequently the inverse comparison sends $(a\otimes s)\otimes(b\otimes t)$ to $ab\otimes(s\otimes t)$: move $a,b$ by linearity and the balancing relation. Its forward rule is $c\otimes(s\otimes t)\mapsto(c\otimes s)\otimes(1\otimes t)$, and the two composites are identities by balancing. The tensor-unit comparison is $\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_T} f^{-1}\mathcal O_T\simeq\mathcal O_X$, $a\otimes r\mapsto a f^\sharp(r)$, with inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. All rules descend from balanced tensors to their sheafifications. Therefore pullback of the homogeneous product has rule $(a\otimes s)(b\otimes t)=ab\otimes(st)$, and the pulled-back unit sends $1$ to $1\otimes1_B$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; normalized scalar-extension comparison and its balanced inverse; tensor unit by multiplication.

proof.text:
For a common chart on which the local tensors in degrees $m,n$ are represented, steps 2 and 4 give
$\epsilon_{m+n}((a\otimes s)(b\otimes t))=ab\,(st)|_W=(a\,s|_W)(b\,t|_W)$,
because the homogeneous products commute with restrictions and are bilinear. Also $\epsilon_0(1\otimes1_B)=1_B$. Bilinearity proves the same identities on finite sums of tensor representatives, and the sheafified tensor universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] makes them equalities of homogeneous module maps. By step 3 these identities on each pair of summands are the multiplicativity identity for $\epsilon$ on the total coproduct; the degree-zero identity gives its unit law. The associativity and ordinary commutativity are the assumed algebra laws under the same tensor rules; there are no cochain signs.

source.place: Tag 0D3C, lemma-descending-property-ample, graded map psi; expanded verification using the local counit and balanced tensor rules of steps 2 and 4.

proof.text:
Now suppose $X$ is a scheme and write $E_Z(M)=M_{\mathrm{et}}$, $R_Z$ for restriction to Zariski opens. By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], $R_XE_XH_d\simeq H_d$, identity on open sections. The right-adjoint comparison of [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square] gives
$A_d=R_T f_{\mathrm{et},*}E_XH_d\simeq f_*R_XE_XH_d\simeq f_*H_d$.
On an open $V\subseteq T$ this is exactly the identity of the sections on $f^{-1}V$. Thus for $s,t$ it sends their product to $st$ on $f^{-1}V$, and sends the pullback of a regular function followed by the unit to that same unit section. This proves the product and unit identifications. Quasi-coherence and the inverse extension comparison are available since the given scheme map is quasi-compact and separated, exactly as required by the two cited statements.

source.place: Tag 03LC, proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial (1),(3); spaces-morphisms.tex discussion preceding lemma-pushforward, ordinary-scheme normalization.

proof.text: The left comparison $E_X f^*\simeq f_{\mathrm{et}}^*E_T$ in [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square] is explicitly the comparison determined by the adjunctions and their units and counits. Hence transposing the etale counit through this square and the identity-on-open-sections right comparison of step 6 gives the identity endomorphism of $f_*H_d$. The ordinary module adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] sends precisely the Zariski counit to that identity. Its injective hom bijection therefore identifies the two counits under the specified comparisons. Concretely, the unit represents a section by $1\otimes s$ on either side, and the counit sends $a\otimes s$ to $a\,s|_W$; thus the statement concerns the fixed normalized maps. Applying the coproduct universal-property calculation of step 3 to the tensor pullbacks $E_X,E_T$ and the two $f^*$ functors shows that all comparisons preserve the summand injections. The equality just proved on each degree therefore identifies the coproduct evaluations as well.

source.place: Tag 03FH, remark-change-topologies-ringed-sites, and Tag 03LC (1),(3): the adjunction comparison square; counits by transposing identities.

proof.text: Finally suppose $B_d=L^{\otimes d}$. The line-module clause of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] gives an ordinary invertible module $H$ with $E_XH\simeq L$. The forward functor $E_X$ is itself the specified ringed tensor pullback. Apply the normalized tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison-construction] and [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison] to it. The tensor-unit map of step 4 gives $E_X\mathcal O_X\simeq\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$ in degree zero. Inductively its binary comparison gives $E_X(H^{\otimes(d+1)})\simeq E_XH\otimes E_X(H^{\otimes d})\simeq L^{\otimes(d+1)}$. In the comparison of degree $m+n$ with degrees $m,n$, each local pure tensor is sent to the same concatenated tensor of $m+n$ factors, by the normalization formula; scalar coefficients multiply on both sides. The tensor universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] therefore identifies the tensor-power products, including the two degree-zero unit products. Restricting these isomorphisms by $R_X$ identifies each corresponding $H_d$ with $H^{\otimes d}$, with these products, as claimed.
